#FloodedVehicleTips

Nakapagrestore na po kami ng flooded vehicles nung ondoy at habagat, kalahating lubog at todo lubog, narerestore pero masalimuot at magastos po sa mga aabutan po ng baha at di mailikas sa higher ground.  Itong BRV todo lubog po yan umabot ng p250k ginastos ng client inorder namin pyesa surplus at sa casa. Yung computer box ni BRV di namin pinalitan nagsurvive.

Sana makatulong itong mga susunod kung Wala kayong insurance acts of nature.

1. Disconnect battery - Kung matatanggal nyo both terminal sa battery tanggalin nyo po bago pa tuluyan tumaas ang floods. 10 or 12 na wrench  kailangan nyo sa stock battery terminal. Kung Wala kayo tools bunutin nyo master fuse sa fuse box

2.  Don't Start your vehicle - Pagkahupa ng baha, hwag na hwag nyo susubukan istart ang sasakyan.  Hindi po Yan tinapa na pwde na kainin agad 😮🤪😭. Pag inistart nyo na damp pa electronics, short circuit ang resulta. At kung nakinig kayo sa amin,  may chance na maaring makuha sa thorough electronics cleaning mga components by a professional or experienced mechanic. Hindi na papalitan.  Tyagaan ang paglinis nyan Isa Isa and test individually.  Also baka mag hydrolock ang engine pwde bumaluktot or magbend ang connecting rods Wala na game over overhaul na makina.

3.  Mga computer box ng vehicles from. Around  2008 onwards sealed and NASA engine bay na sealed in most cases it will survive the floods Basta hwag istart until malinis lahat. Yung ibang critical components hindi sealed at  maaring mag cause ng failure to start engine Kasi flood damaged  like instrumentation panel, throttle position sensor, mass air flow sensor, electric power steering module, Aircon module, electric power steering motor, airbag module, immobilizer module so need malinis or replace if damaged na even after cleaning 

4.  Hubad -Depende sa level ng baha kung Todo lubog eh hubad lahat ng components ng sasakyan Kasi bobombahin Yan ng pressure washer and steam cleaner. Kung kalahating lubog kalas dashboard carpet upuan sidings para malinis pati wiring harness and connectors  Need kalasin Yan Kasi putik Yan pag natuyo may cause rust at Amoy kanal saskyan nyo. All exposed metal structure like safety beam sa ilalim ng dashboard na walang paint need pahiran ng light coat ng oil para madeter ang rust

5. Towing - asahan nyo bukas pahirapan. Ang typical towing rate b4 typhoon Karina nasa  p3K MManila and p4K Rizal expect na tataas Yan. Law of supply and demand.

6.  Pyesa / Parts - typical ordering ng parts sa casa sa Toyota Mitsubishi and Honda based on experience if walang parts sa planta 30 days galing pa Thailand or Japan. “The intense flooding we are now experiencing in Metro Manila, Bulacan, Cavite and Bataan is a direct result of the massive reclamation in Manila Bay,” pahayag ni Kalikasan Advocacy Officer at AKAP KA Manila Bay spokesperson Jonila Castro.

Matapos ang serye ng matinding tag-init, nakararanas naman ngayon ng malawakang pagbaha ang Metro Manila, Bulacan, Cavite, at Bataan na dulot ng pagpasok ng Bagyong Carina sa Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) nitong Lunes, Hulyo 22. 

Kung babalikan ang kalilipas lamang na State of the Nation Address ni Marcos Jr., nangako lamang ito ng pagpapatayo ng “mahahalagang imprastruktura” upang aniya’y magsilbing proteksyon at sentro ng koordinasyon sa paghahatid-tulong. Gayundin ay ang kaniyang pagpupursigi pa sa proyektong reklamasyon sa Pampanga Bay at Cagayan de Oro River na umano’y magsisilbing dagdag lunas sa mga pagbaha. 

Mula pa man 2014, ilang grupo na ng mga eksperto at environmental defenders ang nagpahayag ng pagtutol sa mga proyektong reklamasyon ni dating pangulong Duterte dahil magdudulot ito ng matinding pagbaha gawa ng pagtaas ng sea levels at/o paglubog ng lupa.

Ayon pa sa Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazard (NOAH) project, ang pangunahing programa sa disaster risk reduction and management ng bansa, ang mga coastal erya gaya ng komunidad ng Manila Bay ay lubhang bulnerable sa pagbaha, kung kaya’t delikado ang proyektong reklamasyon at dredging sa mga komunidad gaya nito.

Sa kabila ng mga datos na inilahad ng syensya at pagtutol ng mga residente sa paligid ng Manila Bay, matibay na pinanindigan ni Duterte ang pagpapahintulot sa 2,500 ektaryang proyekto ng kaniyang kroni na San Miguel Corporation (SMC) sa reklamasyon at dredging projects sa Manila Bay. Mayroon pa itong 23 ongoing projects sa 47,000 ektarya na sumisira sa mga likas na yamang tubig at lupa na pumoprotekta sa komunidad mula sa storm surges, pagbaha, at coastal erosions o tuluyang pagguho ng baybayin.

Ganito ang sitwasyon sa Taliptip sa bayan ng Bulakan, Bulacan, na sentro ng malaking reklamasyon ng SMC kung saan ginagawa ang New Manila International Airport na bahagi ng Bulacan Aerotropolis ni Ramon Ang.

Ayon sa mga residente, mula nang magsimula ang proyektong ito ay malaki ang naging perwisyo nito sa kanila lalo sa tuwing tatamaan ng bagyo ang lugar. Nariyan ang mabilis na pagtaas ng tubig, mabagal na paghupa ng baha, at umaabot na sa leeg ng tao ang lebel ng tubig kapag may bagyo.

Ganito rin ang kalagayan sa Navotas kung saan mayroong 650-ektaryang Navotas Bay Reclamation project ang SMC at Navotas LGU. Batid ng mga residenteng mangingisda na may malaking kinalaman ang proyektong ito kung bakit mas matindi ang pagbaha sa Navotas at buong National Capital Region. 

Habang sa CAMANAVA naman, bagamat Signal No. 1 pa lamang kaninang umaga ng Hulyo 24, ay may malawakan nang pagbaha. Anang Bayan Muna Partylist CAMANAVA, na ang paglala ng mga natural disaster nitong mga nagdaang taon ang bunga ng krisis sa klima buhat ng mabilisang pagkalala ng panahon at pagbago ng  temperatura sa buong daigdig.

Lahat ng ito ay sa kabila ng isinaad ni Marcos Jr. sa kaniyang SONA na sa nagdaang dalawang taon ay nakapagtapos ang kaniyang termino ng 5,500 flood control projects.

“From Presidents Duterte to Marcos Jr., lie upon lie has been rained upon us on the so-called benefits of reclamation. And now, only two days after President Marcos Jr.’s State of the Nation Address where he proudly committed himself as a climate champion, all his empty promises are literally drowning homes and families around Manila Bay,” ani Castro.

Sa karagdagan, sa pinuntahang Board of Fund meeting ni Marcos Jr. noong Hulyo 9-12 sa Songdo, South Korea, nakuha ng Pilipinas ang hosting bid sa Loss and Damage Fund (LDF) na isang piskal na mekanismo upang suportahan ang mga developed at developing countries na lubhang naaapektuhan ng climate change.

Ani Lidy Nacpil, coordinator ng Asian Peoples' Movement on Debt and Development (APMDD), nakasalalay na sa Pilipinas bilang host ng LDF kung paano nito ipapamalas ang pamumuno habang bahagi ng Board ng Fund. Dagdag pa ni Nacpil, nararapat na singilin at managot ang mga developed countries sa kanilang “historical, legal, and moral obligation to provide reparations for climate devastation.”

Ayon naman sa isang independent research group na Climate Change Tracker, mula 2022, ang China at United States ang may pinakamalaking ambag sa greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) at pandaigdigang polusyon mula sa naglalakihang kumpanyang gumagamit ng fossil fuel, chemical waste ng mga plantation, at military waste na nagkokontrol sa pagtaas-baba ng temperaturang salik sa krisis sa klima.

“Our experience with Typhoon Carina is showing us that reclamation is a huge lie perpetuated by big business and their partners in government! These projects are not solutions but massive problems. Reclamation projects cause severe flooding and destroy the homes and livelihoods of the people. Those behind these projects must be held accountable,” anang Castro. “Their negligence and disregard for the environment and the welfare of the people must be brought to justice. We will no longer tolerate the continuous destruction of our environment and the exploitation of our communities!,” dagdag pa niya.

Samantala, nakatakdang umalis ng PAR ang bagyo sa Huwebes, Hulyo 25, ngunit mararamdaman ang malakas na ulang dulot nito hanggang Biyernes. Matindi na rin agad ang pinsalang naidulot nito at mas pinalakas ng hanging Habagat sa mga lugar sa Central Luzon at Mindanao kung saan may mga naitalang landslides, at malalaking bilang ng mga pinalilikas. Dagdag pa rito ang pagpapakawala ng ilang mga dam ng tubig kasabay ng pagtaas ng tubig sa mga ilog at look. 

Sa kasalukuyan, idineklara na ng Metro Manila Council (MMC) ang NCR na nasa ilalim ng State of Calamity dahil sa walang tigil na pag-ulan mula noong Lunes. Umabot na rin sa 20.6 meters ang tubig sa Marikina River habang ang La Mesa dam sa Bulacan ay nasa critical level na rin at ang overflowing nito ay nakakaapekto sa mga kalapit na lugar na Quezon City, Valenzuela, at Malabon.

Flooded Car? Here's what to do:

1. Immediately disconnect the negative cable of your car battery to avoid any possible short circuit. This is also to protect the ECU or computer box from damage.

2. Do not start the engine. Try to push the car out to higher ground or try jacking it with the car jack.

3. Disengage and release the parking brake. Keep the transmission in 1st gear (for manual transmission) or "P" (for automatic transmission) to prevent the brake canvas from sticking. This is even more important for cars that use drum brakes.

4. Take plenty of photos both inside and outside the car to document any damage or how deep the car was underwater. This will be useful for both the Insurance and/or Professional Mechanic to determine the extent of the damage.

5. Wait at least 24 hours before you do anything to the vehicle, giving it time to drain, if not completely dry out.

6. If the water got so deep that the dashboard was covered, do not try to start it at all. If any liquid is in the cylinders it will cause damage to the engine. Most of the electronics in the car would have been submerged at this depth, as well.

7. If you don’t think the water got that high, it’s still best to take a look at the oil dipstick to see if there are any traces of water in the lubrication system. If so, assume the engine is flooded and don’t try to start it.

8. You’re in better shape if the water stayed below the center line of your wheels. Nevertheless, let the interior air out as much as possible before trying to start it, taking out the floor mats, trunk mat and even the seats. Much of the wiring and some of the computers in today’s cars are located under the carpet and console box, so even if the engine compartment was not inundated, you could still experience faults to secondary systems.

9. When in doubt, either have your vehicle towed to your trusted service center or call your professional mechanic/electrician for a more thorough inspection and assessment.

Typhoon Carina, combined with the Hanging Habagat, has caused significant flooding in various areas. We are deeply concerned for the safety and well-being of everyone affected. Please take note of the following safety measures to protect yourself and your loved ones during this challenging time:

🚨 Before the Flood:
1.) Stay Informed: Keep updated with the latest weather reports and advisories from official sources like PAGASA and local government units.
2.) Emergency Kit: Prepare an emergency kit with essentials such as water, non-perishable food, medicines, flashlight, batteries, and important documents.
3.) Evacuation Plan: Know the nearest evacuation centers and routes. Plan how to reach them quickly if necessary.
4.) Home Preparation: Secure your home by sealing cracks, ensuring proper drainage, and moving valuables to higher ground.
5.) Turn Off Utilities: Familiarize yourself with the locations of your main switches for gas, electricity, and water.

🌊 During the Flood:
1.) Stay Indoors: If safe, stay inside your home and move to higher floors if necessary. Avoid floodwaters at all costs.
2.) Follow Instructions: Adhere to the advice and instructions given by local authorities and emergency services.
3.) Emergency Kit: Keep your emergency kit within reach and ensure all family members know its location.
4.) Stay Connected: Ensure your mobile phones are fully charged and have backup power sources to stay in touch with family and emergency services.
5.) Avoid Floodwaters: Do not walk or drive through floodwaters as they may be deeper and more dangerous than they appear.

⚠️ After the Flood:
1.) Wait for Clearance: Only return to your home once authorities have declared it safe to do so.
2.) Inspect Your Home: Check for structural damage before entering. Ensure that there are no electrical hazards.
3.) Sanitation: Avoid contact with floodwaters as they may be contaminated. Clean and disinfect everything that got wet.
4.) Health Precautions: Seek medical attention if you have any health concerns or injuries. Be aware of potential waterborne diseases.
5.) Document Damage: Take photos of any damage for insurance claims and assistance applications.

Our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by the flooding.
